title: Contract Drift Detector: synthetic reference corpus and CI guardrails for streaming, tool-calls, and structured outputs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: We continue to see intermittent API compatibility regressions across streaming, function/tool calling, and structured outputs after runtime changes and model shims. Existing golden-seed suites catch many cases but are brittle and expensive to maintain; they also lack focused delta-detection for slow drift (small behavioral changes that slowly increase downstream schema errors).\n\nGoal: Build a lightweight Contract Drift Detector (CDD) that combines a curated synthetic reference corpus ("reference prompts"), deterministic contract tests for API surface compatibility, and CI guardrails that signal: (a) hard breakages (fail builds), (b) measurable drift (annotated warnings in PRs), and (c) triage telemetry for flaky/non-deterministic cases. The CDD must cover streaming response framing, tool/function calling contract semantics (order of events, metadata fields), and structured-output schema fidelity (JSON NDJSON fragments, trailing partial chunks) while minimizing flakiness and runtime cost.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A curated synthetic reference corpus (~250 prompts) covering edgecases for streaming interleaving, tool-calls with nested tool calls, and structured-output partial frames exists in repo and is schema documented.
A2: A set of deterministic contract tests (CI jobs) that run in <6m for fast PR gating and flag hard contract violations with clear failure messages.
A3: CI produces a drift score report (per-test delta vs baseline) and annotates PRs with summary: pass/fail/drift(+score) and links to failing traces.
A4: Non-deterministic failures are auto-classified and queued into a 'flaky' queue with links for manual triage; flaky rate threshold <2% on main branch.
A5: Playbook documenting how to add prompts, update baselines, and approve acceptable drift (owners, criteria, rollback steps) lives in /docs/cdd-playbook.md.
A6: Integration tests cover at least 3 model variants and both hosted and dedicated routing shim layers (router + fallback) in a smoke matrix.
A7: Minimal performance overhead — tests use short timeouts and token limits; overall CI cost delta budgeted in release notes.
technical_notes: Architecture: CDD consists of (1) reference corpus repo, (2) deterministic contract runner (python harness that replays protocol events and asserts contract invariants), (3) CI orchestration: fast-gate (unit-time ~<6m) and extended nightly runs for deeper fuzzing.

Determinism strategy: pin seeds, use stubbed timeouts for streaming, capture event-level fingerprints (event type + sequence id + canonicalized payload) to compare instead of raw token sequences to tolerate model tokenization differences.

Comparison heuristics: exact-match for required fields (tool name, call id, top-level schema keys), tokenized-similarity thresholds for free-text fields, and structural diffs for NDJSON fragments (allow reordering within arrays only when marked 'unordered').

Handling partial/chunked structured output: implement chunk-assembler that tolerantly rehydrates NDJSON from partial stream frames and asserts final schema. Fail early on malformed JSON fragments or missing final terminator token.

False-positive mitigation: maintain per-test expected-variance metadata. When drift score < threshold, CI annotates PR but does not fail; the score contributes to a rolling weekly drift metric used by owners to decide baseline updates.
Telemetry: record failure class (hard-break | drift | flaky | infra) and fingerprint for triage dashboard (Link: https://dashboards.internal.redwood.ai/cdd).
Cross-layer coverage: tests exercise outer API shim (stream framing), toolcall marshalling/unmarshalling, and structured-output validators used by Console and SDKs.
Rollout plan: land harness opt-in on dev branch -> enable fast-gate on core infra PRs -> enable on all runtime PRs after 2 weeks of stabilization.

notes_for_reviewers: Please inspect the corpus mapping file (tests/corpus_map.csv) in PR #12 and add edgecases you hit in recent incidents.
When evaluating drift thresholds, prefer conservative settings for structured-output schema keys; we can be more permissive for free-text fields.
If you are an SDK or Console owner, add expected schema invariants to /specs/cdd-schema.md before the first baseline freeze.
